chapters.title: Visit
paragraphs: Kiro was standing in the middle of his house.
A couch sat in the middle of the living room. An old coffee table stood in front of it, covered in scratches. A blanket had been thrown over one side of the couch and never properly folded again.
A few crooked pictures hung on the walls.
Small shelves held things Kiro probably should have thrown away years ago.
For a second, he looked surprised.
He glanced around himself, almost embarrassed.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “I'm Kiro. Welcome to my house.”
His smile became a little wider.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “I don't know how you got here, but...”
His tail moved slowly behind him.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “I'm glad someone came to visit.”
For a moment, he looked genuinely happy.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “Nobody visits me very often.”
The kitchen was on the right side of the room, connected directly to the living room by a short counter.
A few plates were drying beside the sink.
Then something appeared above the kitchen.
For a few seconds, he didn't move.
Kiro stopped at the entrance to the kitchen.
The counter looked taller than it should.
The floor felt wrong beneath his feet.
The living room behind him was gone.
Two black figures stood near the counter.
One of them could barely stand straight.
A bottle hung loosely from one hand.

runs.text: “Look at yourself. You can barely fucking stand.”

paragraphs: The bottle moved slightly as the figure pointed at her.
Kiro stood only a few steps away.
Neither of them looked at him.
The second figure shook her head.

runs.text: “You're too fucking useless to do anything.”

paragraphs: The second figure tried to move away.

runs.text: “Don't you fucking walk away from me.”

paragraphs: The drunk figure tightened its grip.
The second figure looked directly at the drunk one.
Her head struck the edge of the counter.
Then blood appeared beneath her head.
His raised paw was still in the air.
His paws moved toward his head.
Kiro grabbed the fur on his head.
His claws scraped against his scalp.
Small drops of blood appeared beneath the fur.
Kiro tore at his hair with both paws.
He nearly fell to his knees.
Then the drunk figure turned toward him.
And passed directly through his body.
The plates were still beside the sink.
There was blood on his cheek.
A kitchen knife was hanging from his paw.
The blade was covered in blood.
He didn't seem to understand why he was holding it.
More of the floor became visible behind him.
At the edge of the kitchen...
something black lay on the floor.
Only part of it was visible.

chapters.title: Air
paragraphs: Kiro was playing his favorite game.
He sat on the couch with his legs pulled slightly toward himself, the controller resting between his paws.
His character walked into another room.
Like something was sitting underneath his ribs.
He rubbed the center of his chest.
Then he looked back at the screen.
Right in the middle of his chest.
His character stood still on the television.
The controller loosened in his paws.
Kiro pressed one paw against his chest.
Kiro opened and closed his paw.
The other paw started doing the same.
His heart suddenly hit his chest.
The game was still making noise.
All he could hear was his heart.
The controller slipped from his paws and hit the floor.
He tried to take a deeper one.
But none of it felt like enough.
Like a wet sponge sitting inside his mouth.
He grabbed the couch to keep himself standing.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “I'm having a heart attack.”
He didn't know what to do.
His thoughts stopped behaving like thoughts.
Then one thought hit harder than the others.

runs.text: If something happens, nobody will know.

paragraphs: His legs felt soft underneath him.
His numb paws struggled with the handle.
Kiro immediately leaned against the sill.
His head pushed toward the open air.
He didn't know if the cold helped.
He didn't know if anything helped.
His shaking paws gripping the window frame.
He whispered it like a fact.
Waiting for something inside him to stop.
Instead, his heartbeat slowly began to change.
Eventually, he realized he was breathing almost normally again.
He stayed against the window anyway.
Afraid that moving would make it come back.
That strange feeling before everything else.
Now, when it starts, he tries to control it.
Most of the time, it works.
When it ended, he would sit quietly for a while.
he didn't manage to sit down.
Black dots appeared around the edges.
When Kiro opened his eyes again, he was lying on the floor.
His cheek pressed against the cold wood.
For a few seconds, he didn't understand why.
Nobody even knew he had been unconscious.
Kiro stayed on the floor for a long time.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “I know what it is now.”
His paw was still shaking slightly.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “It's not like the first time.”
He looked toward the place where he had collapsed.
Kiro picked the controller up from the floor.
He sat back on the couch.
The game had been paused for a long time.
Kiro looked down at the controller.
His thumb rested over one of the buttons.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “...I'd still be the only one here.”
He continued exactly where he had left off.

chapters.title: Wrong
paragraphs: Kiro stood in front of the bathroom mirror.
His fur was still damp. Water ran slowly from his ears, down his neck, across his chest.
His fur sat nicely even while wet.
His shoulders had a good shape.
There was nothing obviously wrong with him.
For a second, it looked like he was going to cover himself.
Instead, he just stood there holding it.
Nobody had ever seen that part of him.
Nobody had told him something was wrong.
Kiro had already done all of that for them.
He wrapped the towel around himself and pulled it tight.
But his reflection was still there.
Like he was trying too hard.
Kiro grabbed the edge of the sink.
Kiro in the mirror looked completely normal.
Because there was nothing obvious enough to point at.
Nothing that explained why he felt so disgusting.
Nothing except the one thing nobody could see.
Kiro looked down at the towel.
Leaving it alone made him feel dirty.
Just to see if maybe this time would be different.

runs.text: Why can't you just be fucking normal?

paragraphs: The bathroom suddenly felt too warm.
He stared at the towel around his waist.
[[speech speaker=kiro]] “Nobody else has to think about this every fucking time.”
At least that was what it felt like.
Everyone else in Kiro's head had bodies that simply worked.
Bodies that didn't make them afraid of being touched.
Bodies that didn't make them wonder what somebody would think the first time they saw everything.
Kiro's claws pressed into the sink.
Nobody had ever seen him naked.
That should have made the problem smaller.
Because nobody had proven him wrong either.
So his head did it for them.
Maybe they would ask what was wrong.
Maybe they would try not to stare.
Maybe they would say it was fine in that careful voice people used when something clearly wasn't.
Something hot rose into Kiro's chest.
He looked directly into the mirror.
[[speech speaker=kiro]] “Everything looks fine until someone gets close enough to actually see you.”
Kiro pressed one paw against his chest.
His claws caught slightly in the wet fur.
[[speech speaker=kiro]] “You couldn't even get this one thing right.”
He struck his chest with the flat of his paw.
His paw stayed against his chest.
A red mark was beginning to show beneath the fur.
For a second, he looked surprised.
Not because he had hit himself.
Because the skin had turned red.
Because now there was something else to hate.
Kiro grabbed the fur on his stomach.
As if there was another body somewhere underneath.
His claws scratched against his skin.
Small marks were visible beneath the fur.
Then his eyes moved down again.
That was still the worst part.
Something he would have to explain one day.
Something another person would eventually notice.
Kiro grabbed the towel hanging beside the sink.
He threw it over the mirror.
For a few seconds, he just stood there.
That made him angrier than anything.
Then a hoodie, even though the house was warm.
He pulled the sleeves over his paws.
Kiro looked toward the covered mirror.
Later that evening, he was sitting on the couch.
The hood pulled over his head now.
If somebody walked into the room, they probably wouldn't notice anything.
That was part of the problem.
Nobody could see what Kiro saw.
Nobody knew that a shower could turn into an inspection.
Nobody knew that sometimes he tried the same thing again even when he already knew it would hurt.
Nobody knew that the idea of somebody eventually seeing him scared him more than being alone did.
Kiro looked down at his paws.
For a moment, he wondered what it would feel like to have a body he didn't have to negotiate with.
To imagine somebody touching him without immediately wondering what they would discover.
Kiro pulled his sleeves farther down.
He leaned back against the couch.
The mirror was in another room.
The towel was still hanging over it.
Kiro could still see himself perfectly.

chapters.title: Redirect
paragraphs: He had been sitting like that for almost twenty minutes.
On the edge of the couch.
His paws rested loosely between his legs. Every few seconds, one finger moved.
The television was on, but Kiro wasn't watching it.
Something played quietly in the background.
There was a knock on the door.
Sleeves covering nearly all of his arms and most of his paws.
Rin stepped inside and closed the door. His eyes moved from Kiro, to the television, then back.
For a while, neither of them said anything.
Kiro went back to staring at the floor.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “I don't mean that kind.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “I don't know how to make it stop.”
Kiro tapped one finger against the side of his head.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “I can be doing absolutely fucking nothing and suddenly I remember something.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “And then it just keeps going. The things they said. The things I said. The things I should've done...”
His claws slowly pressed into his palms.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “The things I didn't do.”
Rin looked down at Kiro's paws.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “And then my fucking head starts telling me what kind of person I am.”
His claws were digging into his palms.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “Why are you apologizing to me?”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “I used to get that.”
He pulled one sleeve farther over his paw.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “You're always wearing it. Even when it's fucking boiling outside.”
More like he had just decided something.
Rin grabbed the end of one sleeve.
Places where the fur had grown differently.
Rin looked at his own arm like it belonged to somebody else.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “Same reason you're sitting here looking like you're about to fucking fall apart.”
Rin ran his thumb over one of the older scars.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “When it gets too loud...”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “...I move it somewhere else.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “What does that even mean?”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “Emotional pain is messy. You can't point at it. You can't measure it. You can't tell where it starts or where it fucking ends.”
His eyes moved back to his arm.
Rin moved one paw slightly, enough to make what he meant clear.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “I didn't say it was good advice.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “You literally just showed me that.”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “I showed you what I do.”
Rin pulled his sleeve back down.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “That's not really an answer.”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “It's the only one I've got.”
The television continued talking behind them.
Neither of them looked at it.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “You just fucking showed me that and now you're saying good?”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “I never said you should copy me.”
For the first time, Rin didn't look like he knew what he was talking about.
He looked down and pulled at the end of his sleeve.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “I'm not very good at helping people.”
Rin pushed him lightly with his shoulder.
They stayed together for a few more hours.
Kiro complained about Rin being terrible at the game.
For a little while, Kiro's head became quiet.
Rin put his paws inside the hoodie pocket.
Finally, Rin nodded toward Kiro's phone.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “Message me if you need something.”
His sleeves completely covered his arms again.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “Forget what I showed you.”
Kiro held his eyes for a moment.
For the first few minutes, Kiro felt fine.
He cleaned the glasses from the table.
Put it back where it belonged.
Kiro put the glass down too hard.
Kiro grabbed the sides of his head.
His claws caught in his fur.
He slid down against the kitchen cabinet and pulled his knees toward his chest.
For several seconds, he didn't move.
Kiro looked at his paw again.
Kiro was sitting on the floor.
Small trails of blood were visible through the fur along his arms.
Kiro rested his forehead against his knees.
For the first time that night...
He barely felt anything at all.

chapters.title: Hours
paragraphs: Only his phone lit his face.
He had been scrolling for a while.
Everyone he could talk to was already asleep.
His thumb hovered over the keyboard.
If Rin was asleep, Kiro didn't want to wake him.

runs.text: Then maybe he just didn't want to talk.

paragraphs: Kiro placed the phone beside him.
Ten seconds later, he picked it up again.
He didn't understand why at first.
Then a tear moved down the side of his face and disappeared into the pillow.
Kiro wiped his eyes with his sleeve.
Trying not to make noise even though there was nobody else in the house.
People who had answered him yesterday.
People who had laughed with him.
Because his head started filling in what wasn't there.
Kiro dropped the phone onto his chest.
He covered his eyes with both paws.

runs.text: What if he had already started answering less?
What if he had said something wrong?
Maybe that joke earlier wasn't funny.
Maybe Rin only laughed because it was awkward.
Maybe every conversation was like that.
Maybe people only tolerated him because telling him to leave would be uncomfortable.
Maybe they talked about him when he wasn't there.
Waiting until they could leave without feeling guilty.

paragraphs: He removed his paws from his face.
The phone screen had turned off.
The kind darkness made when you stared into it for too long.
Movement that disappeared whenever his eyes tried to follow it.
Another looked like somebody standing in the corner.
His heart was beating harder now.
He knew there was nothing in the room.
Now he could see things more clearly.
Kiro standing somewhere behind everyone else while they continued without him.

runs.text: They only stay because they feel bad for you.

paragraphs: His fingers tangled into the fur on his head.

runs.text: He saw what you're actually like.
You think he'll keep dealing with this?

paragraphs: He stared into the darkness above him.
But it looked like it did.
The corners of the room bent strangely.
Black shapes crawled across the walls.
His claws pressed into his scalp.
[[speech speaker=kiro]] “Please just shut the fuck up.”
Every stupid thing he had ever said.
Every person who stopped talking to him.
It felt like he had been lying there forever.
At some point, Kiro started crying again.
At some point, his head began hurting.
At some point, he was sitting instead of lying down.
For several seconds, he didn't move.
A deep soreness across his scalp.
Kiro slowly lifted one paw and touched it.
The phone slid from his chest onto the mattress.
he couldn't remember much of the night at all.
He remembered being on his phone.
His knuckles were scraped, with a little dried blood caught in the fur.
A large dark mark covered part of his thigh.
For a few seconds, he just stared.
Then the strands of fur scattered across the pillow.
That felt like five minutes ago.
But hours had disappeared somewhere between then and now.
His thumb hovered over the keyboard.
Kiro looked at his scraped paw.
At the bruise on his leg.
At the fur on his pillow.
He sat on the edge of the bed for a while.
But whatever happened during those missing hours...
Kiro couldn't remember enough of it to be afraid.

chapters.title: Second
paragraphs: Kiro was sitting in the open window.
His back rested against the frame while both legs hung over the roof.
The tiles were cold beneath him.
Most of the windows had already gone dark.
He looked down at the street.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “I just like sitting here.”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “You say that like you've tested it.”
Rin climbed into the window beside him and carefully let his own legs hang outside.
For a moment, they just looked at the street.
Then Rin reached into the pocket of his hoodie.
Kiro heard the small sound before he saw anything.
For half a second, the roof disappeared.
Rin breathed the smoke away from him.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “You want me to put it out?”
He wasn't going to tell Rin what he could and couldn't do just because his own head had attached memories to a smell.
Every few seconds, the smell reached him again.
Every few seconds, something old moved inside his head.
After a while, Rin looked toward him.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “You're annoying as fuck when you're comfortable.”
Rin finished the cigarette and stood up.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “Thank you for telling me.”
Kiro raised one paw without looking at him.
Then he noticed the pack on the windowsill.
He wasn't talking to anyone in the house.
He looked back at the pack.
Turned it over in his paw.
Then he picked it up again.
Remembered coughing so hard his eyes watered.
He remembered saying it was disgusting.
His thumb moved over the cardboard.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “Don't quote me on that.”
He remembered almost nothing about the first one.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “This is a terrible idea.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “That's usually how the bad shit starts.”
A little later, smoke left his mouth.
The cigarette stayed between his fingers.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “I know how fucking stupid this looks.”
But now something else was mixed into it.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “I leave for two minutes.”
Rin climbed back into the window and sat beside him.
For a moment, neither of them spoke.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “This is my second one.”
Rin took another cigarette for himself.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “You're seriously gonna keep going?”
Kiro looked at the burning cigarette.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “I was gonna give it back.”
Two tiny points of light in the dark.
After a while, Rin leaned back against the frame.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “You ever think about how fucking weird life is?”
Rin watched the smoke disappear above them.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “You spend years thinking something is gonna happen. Then it doesn't.”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “Or it happens completely differently.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “Or something happens and you spend years wishing it didn't.”
Kiro looked down at his arm.
The same arm he'd hurt after Rin showed him his scars.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “How much time do you have?”
This one didn't make him cough.
He wasn't sure if that was good.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “I regret shit I did. Shit I didn't do. Things I said. Things I didn't say.”
Rin bumped his shoulder against Kiro's.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “Sometimes I think people expect some big answer.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “Like there's supposed to be a moment where everything makes sense.”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “Kiro... who the fuck are you talking to?”
Rin pointed toward the empty room.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “You were looking directly over there.”
He went back to watching the street.
Kiro looked at you one last time.
The smell still carried memories he didn't want.
it wasn't exactly the same smell anymore.
Kiro wasn't sure how he felt about that.
Kiro looked at what was left between his fingers.
Kiro rested his head against the window frame.
Neither of them talked for a while.
The smoke disappeared into the night.
Kiro watched until he couldn't tell which part had come from Rin...
and which part had come from him.

chapters.title: Still
paragraphs: Rin called it a small birthday party.
Kiro stood in front of the mirror with both paws on his bow tie.
He had bought it that morning.
That meant Rin wanted him there.
Kiro grabbed his jacket and left before his head could argue.
The moment Rin opened the door, Kiro understood that they had very different definitions of small.
Someone walked through the hallway carrying drinks.
Two people were arguing about something near the couch.
More voices came from the kitchen.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “How many fucking friends do you have?”
His tail stayed close to his legs.
Rin noticed the bow tie almost immediately.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “You bought a fucking bow tie?”
But his paw touched the bow tie again.
Just to make sure it was straight.
For the first twenty minutes, Kiro stayed close to Rin.
If Rin walked into the kitchen, Kiro eventually ended up there too.
If Rin joined another conversation, Kiro stayed close enough to listen.
He smiled when somebody looked at him.
Laughed when he was supposed to.
Inside, every voice felt slightly too loud.
Someone touched his shoulder while passing.
Then Rin disappeared into another conversation.
Everything became black shapes with white outlines.
But it sounded far away now.
Like it was coming through several walls.
Shapes changed their outlines into red.
His glass stayed frozen between his paws.
His breathing became so shallow it was almost nothing.
The crowd became one black mass.
Kiro stared at one point at wall.
Rin noticed him from across the room.
He stepped directly in front of him.
Rin slowly reached out and touched his shoulder.
The glass nearly slipped from his paws.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “What the fuck is this?”
Rin took him into a small spare bedroom.
Kiro sat on the edge of the bed.
Messy black hair, short enough to stay around her jaw.
She held a bottle of water.
[[speech speaker=unknown to=kiro]] “He got distracted because somebody can't find the cake knife.”
She walked closer and placed it near his paw.
Something uncomfortable moved inside Kiro's chest.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Mostly that you're an asshole.”
His claws struggled slightly with the cap.
Susie sat on the chair across from him.
One curl hanging over her eye.
Something warm moved through Kiro's chest
His grip tightened around the bottle.
For half a second, Susie disappeared.
A phone was in his paw.
[[message speaker=unknown to=kiro]] Can I talk to you?
[[message speaker=unknown to=kiro]] I really need you right now.
[[message speaker=unknown to=kiro]] You're the only person who understands.
Then Kiro typing something about himself.
[[message speaker=unknown to=kiro]] anyway can I call you?
He hated that he liked it.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Kiro, you're breathing really fast.”
His voice came out sharper than he meant.
Kiro put the water down before he dropped it.
Rin came in carrying another glass of water.
The glass immediately went onto the desk.
Kiro had one paw pressed against his chest.
Rin crouched in front of him.
His breathing was already too fast.
Rin reached for one of his paws.
Rin didn't say anything about it.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “It doesn't fucking feel like it.”
Kiro had told him about the attacks before.
Sometimes feeling like he was going to die.
Knowing about it was different from sitting directly in front of him while it happened.
Kiro's fingers tightened around his paw.
Two fingers rested against Kiro's wrist.
For half a second, something changed in his face.
He didn't want Kiro seeing him panic too.
Kiro's claws extended without him noticing.
Far enough not to crowd him.
Then somewhere behind both of them.
Black dots appeared around the edges of everything.
He caught Kiro under the arms before his head could hit the floor.
For one horrible second, Rin just stared at him.
A few seconds earlier, Kiro had been dragging in breath after breath.
Like none of it was enough.
Like his body had simply switched the panic off the moment Kiro lost consciousness.
Rin knew he wasn't convincing either of them.
A moment ago he had looked like he was fighting for air.
Rin kept hold of his paw.
Kiro came back a couple of minutes later.
One paw wrapped around Kiro's paw.
Two fingers resting against his wrist.
For just a second, relief showed on his face.
She gave him a small smile when she noticed he was properly awake.
He was still watching Kiro's face.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “You know where you are?”
Rin's fingers stayed against his wrist.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “You know why you're here?”
Kiro looked down at their paws.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “It was fucking ridiculous before.”
But nowhere near what it had been.
The sentence seemed to remind him of everything at once.
Rin sitting here instead of with them.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “You were unconscious like two minutes ago.”
Then he heard someone laugh outside.
He covered his face with his free paw.
Rin kept his fingers against Kiro's wrist.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “I fucking passed out at your birthday.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “You had to bring me in here.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “You had to fucking sit here with me.”
Rin glanced down at his own paw.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “And Susie had to stay too.”
Rin felt Kiro's pulse speed up slightly again.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “Doing that thing where you apologize until you make yourself worse.”
For half a second, Kiro almost smiled.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “Because five minutes ago your heart felt like a fucking machine gun.”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “You didn't say I was gonna feel it trying to escape through your wrist.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “You left everyone because of me.”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “I walked into another room.”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “Because you're my friend and you collapsed.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “You should be out there.”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “I'm where I want to be.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “You didn't have to stay.”
Something warm moved through his chest.
He stared down at the blanket.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “Please shut the fuck up.”
Kiro gave a broken little laugh.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “You're alive enough to insult me. That's progress.”
Kiro wiped quickly at one eye before either of them could mention it.
Rin never fully stopped watching him.
Sometimes his eyes went to Kiro's chest.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “Can you stop looking at me like that?”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “Like I'm gonna fucking explode.”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “After trying to inhale the entire room.”
His breathing was completely normal now.
Around fifteen minutes after the attack, he looked almost normal.
That was the strangest part for Rin.
He reached for Kiro's wrist again.
His breathing had become normal almost immediately after he collapsed.
Now his heart finally matched it.
Rin stayed there for another few seconds anyway.
Rin looked at his wrist again.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “Fifteen minutes ago your heart felt like it was trying to punch through your skin.”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “And now you're just sitting here.”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “I knew you got attacks.”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “I knew your heart went fast.”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “I knew you sometimes passed out.”
Rin rubbed the back of his neck.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “I don't even wanna know what that feels like.”
Then Rin looked at him differently.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “You usually deal with that alone?”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “You handle it better than I would.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “This isn't exactly a success story.”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “But you're sitting here fifteen minutes later making shitty jokes and arguing with me.”
Rin wasn't sure whether that was impressive or horrible.
Kiro pulled the bow tie loose.
He hated how much he liked hearing it.
He pulled the bow tie off completely.
Held it in his paws for a moment.
And put it in his pocket.

chapters.title: Tracks
paragraphs: The party was still going when Kiro decided to leave.
Rin was arguing with somebody about whether the cake had been cut evenly.
Kiro stood near the front door with his jacket already on.
Everything was normal enough that nobody looking at him would know what had happened less than an hour ago.
Rin noticed him putting his shoes on.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “My heart isn't exploding. I can breathe. I know what room I'm in.”
The bow tie was still folded inside his pocket.
He could feel it when his paw brushed against his jeans.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “Message me when you got home.”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “Because if you don't I'm gonna assume you collapsed in a ditch somewhere.”
Then a voice came from behind him.
Susie was standing a few steps away.
Jacket thrown loosely over it now.
Her messy black hair looked even messier than before.
Kiro raised one paw without turning around.
Kiro normally reached Rin's house through the urban part of town.
Susie walked beside  him for maybe two minutes before pointing toward a smaller road.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You know there's another way, right?”
Kiro looked where she was pointing.
The road disappeared between a few houses and continued toward the trees.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “There's an old railway line through it. Goes almost all the way toward your side of town.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “How do you know where I live?”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “It's nicer than the road.”
The sun was already low, turning everything orange between the clouds.
Tiny drops of rain were beginning to fall.
Kiro looked toward the trees again.
The kind of weather he would normally choose on purpose.
The tracks appeared a few minutes later.
Or what was left of them.
Grass grew between the wooden sleepers.
Some sections were almost completely buried.
The forest was quiet except for the rain touching the branches above them.
Kiro walked directly between the rails.
Susie walked on one of them for a few steps, arms slightly out of balance.
Kiro looked away before she could see him smile.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I have no idea what you're talking about.”
Susie jumped down from the rail.
For a while, neither of them spoke.
Silence with someone else usually made his head start working.
Kicked a wet leaf off one of the tracks.
Stopped once to look at a mushroom growing beside an old sleeper.
He shoved both paws into his jacket pockets.
His fingers touched the bow tie.
Kiro pulled his paw away from it.
A drop of rain landed directly on Kiro's nose.
Kiro looked up through the branches.
The forest became darker as the sun dropped.
Somewhere ahead, the tracks crossed an old road that hadn't been used in years.
A railway barrier still stood beside it.
One side hung permanently lowered across nothing.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “We've been walking for like twenty minutes.”
She sat on the old barrier.
The metal was cold even through his jeans.
For a moment, they said nothing.
Dark rails disappearing in both directions.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Are you always that nervous?”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “What am I supposed to say?”
Kiro looked back toward the tracks.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Maybe he's stealing my material.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “I'm not saying that to make you feel bad.”
Kiro rubbed his thumb against the edge of his sleeve.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I don't usually have that happen around people.”
Susie didn't ask what he meant.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I normally deal with this alone.”
Susie looked down the railway line.
No speech about how he shouldn't be alone.
No promise that she'd always be there.
Kiro liked that answer more than he probably should have.
The rain tapped quietly against the barrier.
She noticed something near his shoe.
A small stone sat between two old sleepers.
One broken edge showed something pale and slightly reflective inside.
Kiro leaned down and picked it up.
He rubbed the dirt away with his thumb.
He looked back at the stone.
Kiro slipped it into his pocket.
The stone settled beside the folded bow tie.
He could feel both when he moved.
Something from tonight he wanted to hide.
Something from tonight he wanted to keep.
Kiro didn't think about that too hard.
They stayed longer than either of them meant to.
Cold started settling between the trees.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “We're really good at this.”
The rest of the walk was darker.
But enough that the forest had lost most of its color.
Wet leaves reflected what little light remained.
Kiro knew the tracks were taking them closer to his house now.
He could recognize some of the surrounding roads through the trees.
They eventually left the forest behind.
Susie looked toward the small house.
For some reason, this part felt harder than the entire walk.
Then at the dark road behind her.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “And you're going through there?”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “What are you gonna do, throw it at a murderer?”
Another small drop of rain landed on his ear.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “You could stay for a bit.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Not like stay, stay. Just until it stops raining or gets less fucking cold or whatever. I have...”

runs.text: She doesn't want to come inside.

paragraphs: The house looked exactly the same as when he had left it.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You really do collect them.”
The house didn't feel as empty with another person standing inside it.
So he went to the kitchen.
They had been there for years.
From the living room, Susie called:
He placed both on the counter.
For a moment, he just looked at them.
Then he started making the hot chocolate.
Susie stayed in the living room.
At least for about thirty seconds.
Then he heard her moving around.
She was standing in front of one of the shelves.
Something dark with thin white lines running through it.
A smooth orange stone Kiro had found years ago and kept even though he wasn't completely sure what it was.
She picked up one of the smaller pieces.
Turned it slowly between her fingers.
She put it back exactly where it had been.
Most people would have just dropped it somewhere on the shelf.
He looked back at the mugs.
The milk was getting too hot.
A few minutes later, he carried both mugs into the living room.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “It's one of the few things I can make without setting something on fire.”
For a moment, they just stood there.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Why does everybody say that to me?”
Kiro looked toward the window again.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “That makes it sound weirder.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “People can murder people upstairs.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Do you think I could murder you?”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “No, it's fine. Great for my confidence.”
He put his mug down for a second and walked toward the window.
Kiro picked his mug back up.
He put one leg through the window.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You're going through the fucking window.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Because the wall is inconvenient.”
The roof beneath the window was wide and fairly flat, only sloping gently toward the edge.
He sat down near the window and looked back inside.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “I'm deciding whether you're fucking with me.”
The last light of the sunset was disappearing behind the forest.
Wet rooftops reflected the streetlights below.
A thin rain moved through the air.
She held a paw out to him.
Her shoe slipped slightly against the wet frame.
For a second, they stood much closer than either of them expected.
Susie picked up her mug again.
For a while she just looked.
The old railway line was somewhere inside it now, hidden beneath the trees.
The rain was light enough that they could hear individual drops hitting the roof.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You come up here a lot?”
Kiro looked back toward the town.
Kiro rubbed one thumb against the warm mug.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “When I wanna be alone.”
Kiro continued before he could decide not to.
Kiro kept his eyes on the distant trees.
He looked down toward the street.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “So I come up here.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “What kind of stupid shit?”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Sometimes I stay until I'm freezing.”
Susie looked toward the horizon again.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “So this is like your secret place?”
Kiro suddenly realized how that sounded.
Susie looked back toward the town.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “I know what you mean.”
Didn't ask why he needed somewhere to be alone.
Didn't ask what he thought about up here.
Then quickly back at the lights below.
He took another sip of hot chocolate.
For once, the thought didn't sound very convincing.

chapters.title: Warm
paragraphs: At first it had only been a few drops hitting the roof around them.
Kiro and Susie were still sitting where they had been before.
The town below was wet and dark.
Farther away, the forest had almost completely disappeared into the evening.
Only the tops of the pines were still visible.
A flash appeared somewhere behind the trees.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I like them when I'm not standing in the middle of one.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “We're sitting on a roof.”
Drops started hitting Kiro's shoulders and running through the fur around his ears.
Susie's hair was getting wet too.
Thunder followed only a few seconds later.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “We've been sitting on a wet roof for how long?”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I thought you liked it.”
Another cold drop landed in Susie's hair.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “I can like it and still be freezing.”
Thunder followed a few seconds later.
Susie stood and looked toward the window.
Kiro stayed seated for another moment.
He looked toward the forest one last time.
Orange and red leaves moved between the dark pines.
Susie climbed through the window first.
Kiro stayed outside for another few seconds.
Then a drop went directly into his eye.
But now there was glass between them and it.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “You planning to go through the forest in that?”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “I was considering my options.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Your options are getting soaked or getting fucking electrocuted.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “You can also get lost.”
Another crack of thunder shook the window slightly.
Kiro rubbed the back of his neck.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “You could just stay here tonight.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “I was going to ask if you're sure.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I mean, unless you really want to walk home through that.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “I think I can survive one night on your couch.”
Something warm moved through his chest.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Unless you want to go directly to sleep at...”
Kiro made himself another hot chocolate.
By the time they sat down, the storm had gotten worse.
Wind moved through the trees outside.
Every few minutes, lightning turned the entire living room white.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “That's exactly what somebody planning a murder would say.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “You know where the door is.”
They sat on opposite sides of the couch.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “It's been like six minutes.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “What did my face say?”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I can choose a fucking movie.”
Less than a minute later, she stopped.
Something badly edited standing behind it.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “If it's good, we watch it.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “If it's bad, we make fun of it.”
Someone on screen slowly walked toward a basement door.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You say that like you wouldn't do the exact same thing.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You climbed through a window onto a wet roof.”
For a while, everything was easy.
He stopped thinking about whether he was talking too much.
Whether she was only staying because the weather forced her to.
A character walked into another obviously dangerous room.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “If he dies, that's his fault.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “He's had seven opportunities to leave.”
At the exact same moment, thunder cracked directly above the house.
Susie looked at him for a second.
Kiro's smile stayed a little longer.
Somewhere around the middle of the movie, Susie shifted.
She shifted farther to her side of the couch.
Kiro stared at the space she had created.
Kiro tried to focus on the movie.
His heart was beating a little faster.
The thunder was close enough now that sometimes only a second or two passed after the lightning.
Kiro didn't even need to look at her this time.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I can feel you smiling.”
When she settled back, she didn't move as far away.
But this time he didn't freeze.
The contact slowly stopped feeling like something he had to monitor.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You passed out at a birthday party like four hours ago. You're not allowed to judge me.”
Kiro realized she hadn't insulted anybody on screen for several minutes.
Her head rested against his shoulder.
Every part of his body suddenly became noticeable.
Her hair lightly touching the side of his face.
Maybe she had done it without thinking.
She was supposed to sleep here anyway.
Tell her to lie down properly.
His shoulder was already becoming uncomfortable.
His mug was on the table, just far enough away that reaching it would move her.
The remote was beside Susie's leg.
He had no idea what was happening anymore.
No midnight message asking him to fix something.
She wasn't crying and telling him he was the only person who understood.
Because she felt comfortable enough to fall asleep beside him.
Something warm moved through Kiro's chest.
Kiro looked back at the television.
The credits started a few minutes later.
The television returned to its menu.
Kiro closed his eyes for a moment.
That wasn't the same as disappearing.
He looked toward the dark window.
Kiro slowly relaxed his shoulder beneath her.
His eyes moved toward the stairs.
Instead, he rested his head against the back of the couch.
louder than everything inside his head.

chapters.title: Quiet
paragraphs: The television glowing quietly across the room.
His phone was on the table.
His grip tightened around the phone.
Kiro threw the phone onto the couch.
Kiro dug his claws into his palms.

runs.text: Everyone has to take care of you.
Can't even make your own head shut up.

paragraphs: His claws dragged across his arms.
More blood appearing through the fur.
He just wanted the noise somewhere else.

runs.text: Rin will get tired of you.
Why would anyone fucking love you?

paragraphs: Blood ran slowly through the fur on his arms.
Something small lay among the papers.
He grabbed the sides of his head.
His mother on the kitchen floor.
Susie walking beside him through the forest.

runs.text: YOU SHOULD HAVE ENDED THIS YEARS AGO.

paragraphs: Kiro stared at the blood on his paws.
Kiro slowly looked toward the stairs.
Where Susie had been sitting only hours ago.
Blood washed slowly from his fur and disappeared between the wet tiles.
Kiro looked down toward the place where Susie had sat.

runs.text: “Because you're my friend and you collapsed.”

paragraphs: A tear moved down his cheek.
Then the ground rushed toward him.
His body hit the ground wrong.
For a moment, everything flashed white.
Blood spread beneath him, thin at first, then mixing with the water across the ground.
The roof was above him now.
The open window looked impossibly small.
Kiro tried to move one paw.
Then the ground beneath him changed.
For a second, he didn't understand.
There was light somewhere above him.
Tried to move anywhere except down.
But the darkness kept taking him.
The voice came from above the water.
The thing around his leg tightened.
Couldn't even tell if he was getting closer anymore.
Kiro stared at the light above him.
Susie's voice kept coming through the water.
The burning in his chest became unbearable.
Blood slowly drifted from his nose.
Then from the corner of his mouth.
Dark clouds spread through the water around his face.
Kiro looked toward the disappearing light.
Wanted to tell her he could hear her.
But he was already too deep.
And Kiro stopped trying to reach it.

chapters.title: Seen
paragraphs: He coughed hard, dragging in another breath like he'd actually been underwater.
The television still glowing across the room.
For a few seconds, he didn't understand.
He could still feel something around his leg.
Still see blood floating through black water.
Susie let out a shaking breath.
His paws immediately went to his arms.
He really was lying beside it.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You were breathing weird. I tried waking you up, then you just...”
He could still hear his own thoughts screaming at him.
Then he noticed she wasn't looking at his face anymore.
One sleeve had been pushed almost completely up when he fell.
Not only the smaller marks his claws sometimes left.
Things she wasn't supposed to know about.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “How much did you see?”
Kiro grabbed the end of his sleeve.

runs.text: She knows what you really are.

paragraphs: Kiro folded forward and covered his face.
The first sob came out suddenly.
He immediately tried to swallow the next one.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I don't want you to see that.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I know how it looks.”
He grabbed the sleeve and pulled it farther over his paw.
Like he could hide what she had already seen.
A horrible little sound between breaths.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “You don't have to fucking lie.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Kiro, I'm not saying anything.”
He pressed both paws against his head.
[[speech speaker=kiro]] “I know, I know, I know...”
His paws were starting to tingle.
His heart slammed against his ribs.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “It doesn't fucking feel like it.”
For a stupid second, like Rin might appear there.
No one who had seen this before.
No one to tell her what she was supposed to do.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I don't want another fucking...”
Susie watched him for another second.
She moved forward and wrapped her arms around him.
His face disappeared against her shoulder.
A sob tore out of him.
He clutched the back of her shirt like she could disappear if he let go.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I don't want you to fucking see me like this.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “You shouldn't have to deal with this.”
Susie felt his whole body shaking against her.
She didn't tell him to calm down.
Didn't tell him everything was fine.
He buried his face deeper against her shoulder, trying to hide while literally holding onto her.
His claws caught slightly against the fabric on her back.
A small broken sound escaped him.
He struggled for enough air to speak.
Kiro held onto her like he already expected her paws to disappear from his back.
Susie lowered her head slightly against his.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “I'm not leaving right now.”
His breathing was still too fast.
Just Susie sitting on the floor beside him.
Kiro's sleeve stayed clenched between them.
He knew she had seen underneath it.
There was no hiding it again.
He cried until the apologies stopped sounding like words.

chapters.title: Watching & Listening
paragraphs: His breathing was still uneven, but the panic had finally started letting go of him.
Susie sat beside him on the floor.
Not holding him anymore, but close enough that their shoulders touched.
Kiro kept one paw wrapped around the end of his sleeve.
He hadn't let go of it since she saw underneath.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “I'm going to the kitchen.”
She watched him for another second.
Kiro wiped his face with his sleeve.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “Don't fucking look at me like that.”
His paw tightened around his sleeve.
Instinctively, he pulled it farther over his wrist.
He stared at what he was doing.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “...Why am I even hiding it from you?”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “She found out five minutes ago.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “You knew before she did.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “How long have you been watching me?”
He leaned back against the couch.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “You always show up for the good parts, huh?”
His tail moved once against the floor.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “You saw me hit the ground.”
His body still remembered it anyway.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “Is this fun for you?”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “Watching me fuck everything up?”
Susie stood at the edge of the room holding a glass of water.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Were you talking to someone?”
She looked toward the empty place Kiro had been staring at.
Her expression said she had several questions.
Apparently she decided none of them were worth asking tonight.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Nearly drowned yourself with water after having a nightmare about drowning.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “...How much did I say?”
He put the glass on the table.
Thunder still rolled somewhere far away, but the storm was moving on.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “We should probably try sleeping again.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I don't really want to.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You planning to sleep there?”
He climbed back onto the couch.
This time there was a little space between them.
The menu music had been looping for so long it was starting to feel threatening.
Susie grabbed the remote and turned it off.
Kiro immediately looked toward the window.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “What if this happens again?”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Then I'll wake you up.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Then I'll wake you up harder.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You don't have to sleep.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “We can just sit here.”
Then at the small space between them.
Slowly, he moved his paw onto the couch between them.
A few seconds later, her paw rested beside his.
Susie turned her head toward him.
Susie watched him for a second.
A few seconds later, she snored again.
Sometimes surprisingly loud for someone her size.
But it meant she was there.
Still comfortable enough to sleep badly.
Another snore came from beside him.
And this time, the snore didn't bother him at all.
For a moment, he didn't know why he was on the couch.
Curled awkwardly against the other side of the couch.
Kiro looked at her phone lying on the table.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Doesn't anyone wonder where you are?”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “I messaged him last night.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “When you were making drinks.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “You told him you were staying here?”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “And he was just fine with that?”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “I told him the storm was bad and I was staying at a friend's place.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “He's not going to send the police after you.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I wasn't worried about that.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “I'm not a child anymore. I don't need permission to sleep somewhere.”
Kiro picked at the edge of his sleeve.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I lived with my father for a long time.”
Kiro hadn't meant to say it.
The words were already there now.
Kiro stared at the dark television.
Kiro gave a small humorless laugh.
He rubbed his thumb against his palm.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Nice family. Helpful family. Normal family.”
His eyes stayed on the television.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “They were good at looking like one.”
Kiro continued before he could decide not to.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “When he drank, he got aggressive.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “He argued with her. Screamed at her. Scared her.”
Like that mattered enough to say quickly.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Made the whole fucking house feel like you were waiting for something.”
Rainwater slowly moved down the outside of the window.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “It was a few months after, I think.”
His eyes narrowed slightly, trying to find the memory.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “She came into my room at night.”
His mother sitting on the edge of his bed.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “She asked me what she should do.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “She said she didn't feel safe there anymore.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “What did you tell her?”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Whatever would make her happier.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I told her if she wanted to leave, she should leave.”
His paw tightened around the fabric of his jeans.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “She lives really far away now.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Other half of the planet kind of far.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Having your mom inside a rectangle.”
Susie looked down at her own phone.
Like he needed that part to be understood.
The answer came harder than everything before it.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “My dad told me it was my fault.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “He knew she'd talked to me.”
His fingers moved against his knee.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “He told me I convinced her.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “That I broke the family.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “He said she left because of me.”
For a long moment, there was only the sound of water dropping from the roof outside.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=reader]] “You knew that too, didn't you?”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “..Who are you talking to?”
His eyes moved back to her.
She decided to leave that alone too.
Kiro rubbed his arms through his sleeves.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “You said your dad knows.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Sorry. You don't have to...”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “We're going to start charging you.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I'll be homeless by Friday.”
For the first time that morning, it didn't hurt.
Hot chocolate for Kiro because apparently morning wasn't enough to stop him.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You drink that for breakfast?”
Orange leaves stuck to the road.
Some had collected against the fence in heavy dark piles.
The trees moved gently in the cold wind.
The sky was still gray, but brighter now.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “At least it stopped raining.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You really like this weather?”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “...You make autumn sounds really depressing.”
Kiro gestured vaguely toward the window.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Cold outside, yet not freezing. Warm inside.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “What  do you even do in autumn?”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Same things I do the rest of the year.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Streets. Buildings. People sometimes. Forests. Stupid little details.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “That's actually kind of nice.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Whatever I like. Old stuff mostly. Things I find by accident.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I might have something you'd like.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “That's also what suspicious people say.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “We'd have to walk a little.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “If you murder me after I survived your couch, I'm going to be really annoyed.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “You snored on that couch.”
Orange leaves covered the pavement and stuck to the edges of the road. Water dripped from roofs and branches. The air was cold enough that Kiro kept his paws partly hidden inside his sleeves.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “So where are we going?”
Across a road covered in wet leaves.
Then Kiro stopped in front of narrow little shop.
The window was filled with old album covers, handwritten price cards, and a few records propped up against the glass.
He opened the door for her.
A small bell rang above it.
Rows of vinyl filled most of the shop.
A record player behind the counter.
The place smelled faintly of old paper, cardboard, dust, and coffee.
Kiro closed the door behind them.
She walked toward the nearest shelf immediately.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I thought you might like it.”
Susie pulled out one record, looked at the cover, then another.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “How do you even know about this place?”
Kiro walked past her toward the counter.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “And you just never mentioned that?”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Kiro, that's not something people normally have to ask.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “What, you don't ask everyone where they work within twenty-four hours of meeting them?”
Then he moved toward one of the shelves.
Kiro crouched beside a lower crate and started searching through it.
Susie stayed nearby, still looking around the shop with the kind of expression Kiro was trying very hard not to look pleased about.
A few boxes that looked like nobody had opened them in years.
Susie watched Kiro flip through the records.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You actually know where everything is?”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “It means don't touch the wrong pile.”
Susie looked toward one particularly questionable stack beside the counter.
A few seconds later, Kiro stopped.
Kiro looked at the cover, then handed it to her.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Do I get to know why?”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I'm trying to prevent you from having the wrong opinion.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “That's not how opinions work.”
Susie followed him, still looking at the record.
A modern turntable set beside a small amplifier and pair of speakers.
It wasn't some ridiculous expensive setup.
He removed it carefully from the sleeve.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You look very serious suddenly.”
Kiro placed it onto the turntable.
He switched everything on, waited for the record to start spinning, then lowered the needle.
