He stared at one of the hot dogs turning slowly beneath the glass.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You were going to eat it anyway.”
Susie added something that claimed to be cheese.
Kiro looked at the little plastic cup.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “So does spray paint if you write it on the can.”
The cashier looked between them while putting everything into a bag.
Probably halfway through a shift she already hated.
The cashier looked at them again.
Kiro just stared at the card reader like it had suddenly become the most important object in the building.
The cashier handed them the bag.
That was all he could produce.
Outside, the cold air hit them again.
Kiro walked beside Susie toward the Ranger.
The plastic bag rustled between them.
Kiro reached for the passenger door.
Kiro rubbed the back of his neck.
Kiro became more uncomfortable with every second.
She leaned against the side of the Ranger.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “If we are, I guess we're supposed to kiss at some point.”
He rubbed one paw against the other.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Why does everyone say that like I've been secretly running around kissing people?”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “I didn't mean it like that.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “But all of it was long distance.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “And all of it crashed into the ground pretty fucking fast, so...”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Unless we're counting my mom and aunts.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “I wasn't going to say anything.”
Susie leaned back against the truck.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “So you never thought about it?”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “What kind of question is that?”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I never really imagined it.”
He looked toward the gas station windows.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I thought about being with someone.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Like actually being with them.”
He rubbed his paw over his arm.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I think every time I got close to imagining anything physical, my brain just went...”
He made small motion with his paw.
His eyes dropped to her mouth.
Susie stayed there for only a moment.
Kiro moved before he thought about it.
His paw caught lightly against her sleeve.
Of the fact that he wanted her to continue.
Susie looked at him for half a second.
This time Kiro knew it was coming.
Still didn't know what to do.
The other hovered uselessly beside him.
Then slowly settled against her side.
Didn't try to make it anything more than it was.
Her paw resting lightly against his chest.
The faint smell of coffee still caught in her jacket.
Kiro forgot about the awful hot dogs in the bag between them.
In reality, probably nowhere near that long.
His eyes stayed closed for another second.
Not enough for Susie to see.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Look at me like that.”
Like he needed to check something.
Kiro looked at her so fast it almost hurt.
Kiro looked down at her again.
Susie picked up the food bag from where she'd placed it against the truck.
Then glanced toward the gas pumps.
Susie handed him the food bag.
Then walked toward the gas station.
The tiny cowboy ghost hanging from the mirror stared at him.
The ghost offered no useful answer.
Kiro leaned back in the seat.
He covered his face with both paws.
Outside, Susie walked back toward the store to pay for the gas.
Kiro stayed exactly where she left him.
Still holding two terrible hot dogs.

chapters.title: Road
paragraphs: The drive home after the gas station was almost completely silent.
Neither of them had enough energy left for awkward.
The concert had destroyed their ears.
The terrible hot dogs had barely counted as food.
He was absolutely thinking about that.
He sat in the passenger seat with his head against the window.
Every few minutes his eyes moved toward Susie.
At some point Kiro noticed the Ranger drifting slowly toward the line.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “For half a fucking century.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I'm not letting you drive farther like this.”
That had been easier than expected.
They barely made it to the couch.
Susie dropped her jacket over a chair.
She pulled the blanket from the back of the couch.
Maybe a minute later, her head rested against his shoulder.
One paw resting loosely near his side.
Susie sat at the kitchen table with messy hair, drinking water and looking like she had personally declared war on consciousness.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “You don't even know what it is.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I want to take you somewhere.”
That woke her up a little.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “It's supposed to be a surprise.”
Kiro looked unusually pleased with himself.
That made her even more suspicious.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You don't even know what I'm asking.”
Kiro glanced through the window toward the Ranger.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You want to drive my truck.”
Kiro rubbed the back of his neck.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Do you have a driver's license?”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Then how the fuck are you planning to drive?”
Kiro rubbed his palms against his jeans.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “When I was little, my dad taught me how to drive a tractor.”
That answer clearly wasn't what she'd expected.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Small enough that I probably shouldn't have been driving a fucking tractor.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “It was one of the few things with him that...”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “He'd sit there and tell me what to do.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Sometimes he'd let me steer.”
Kiro rubbed his thumb against his palm.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I remember liking the machine.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Not really everything around it.”
Kiro looked toward the truck again.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I haven't driven anything in years.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I remember how it works.”
He stepped closer to the table.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “We'd only be on normal roads for a little bit.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Then it's mostly forest roads.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I want to show you this place.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I haven't been in there in...”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I barely remember the way.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “But I remember the place.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “And I know you'll like it.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You really want to do this.”
That didn't make the decision easier.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “If I tell you to stop, you stop.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “If I think you're doing something stupid, we're switching.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “And if you crush my truck...”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I'll die before you can kill me.”
She dropped the keys into it.
His smile disappeared for a second.
The weight of them suddenly made everything real.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Just give me a second.”
Kiro put both paws on the wheel.
For a moment, he wasn't twenty-five.
For a few seconds, the controls felt unfamiliar.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Means you're not stupid enough to think you're good at this.”
Kiro slowly backed the Ranger out.
Late enough that most people had already gone to work.
Early enough that the roads still felt quiet.
Kiro drove like every mailbox was waiting to jump in front of him.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You know you can go faster than fifteen.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “I didn't mean funeral procession.”
A few streets later, they reached the edge of town.
But less like operating alien machinery.
Then he turned off the paved road.
A narrow dirt path disappeared between the trees.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “This is where you murder me.”
He shifted slightly in his seat.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Whole thing was very elaborate.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “All part of the plan.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Now I murder us both on a tree.”
The Ranger bounced over the first rough section.
Susie grabbed the handle above the door.
Potholes that looked old enough to have names.
The Ranger rocked from side to side.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Maybe don't destroy my suspension.”
No signs except occasional faded markers Kiro barely remembered.
Something about one path felt familiar.
After another few minutes, the path became smoother.
Kiro relaxed enough to press a little more.
The Ranger moved through the forest.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Remembering something with him and not immediately hating it.”
Kiro rubbed one thumb against the steering wheel.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Children famously hate big machines.”
He took one paw briefly away from the wheel.
Held it above the center console.
Susie stared at his waiting paw.
Same place hers had been on the drive to the concert.
Then put her paw into his.
Then he let go and put his paw back where it belonged.
Branches scraped lightly along the sides of the Ranger.
Something had appeared between the trees.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I actually fucking found it.”
The road opened into a small clearing.
Beyond it, through the trees, water.
And near the edge of the clearing stood an old watchtower.
Tall enough to rise above the trees.
Some boards looked newer than others.
Only wind moving through the trees.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You knew this was there?”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I wasn't even sure it still existed.”
Susie's eyes moved toward the lake.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Get out of the truck.”
Susie was already walking toward the tower.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I'll take that as yes.”
The tower disappeared into the branches above them.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You brought me to an abandoned watchtower beside a lake.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I knew you'd like it.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Places nobody else gives a shit about.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Was that supposed to be romantic?”
Then she reached for his paw.
Susie looked toward the tower again.

chapters.title: Tower
paragraphs: Kiro made it maybe ten steps.
Kiro stared back toward the Ranger.
Susie looked at her empty shoulder.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I brought you to a lake in the middle of nowhere, found an old watchtower, and left your camera bag in the truck.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You don't have to run!”
He reached the Ranger, opened the passenger door and grabbed her camera bag from behind the seat.
Then noticed the smaller pouch beside it.
When he came back, he was slightly out of breath.
Susie was waiting beneath the tower.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “In case you want pictures from the top.”
The tower was much worse from underneath.
Four tall wooden supports rose above them, connected by heavy crossed beams.
A staircase zigzagged through the open structure.
At the very top sat a small wooden cabin, windows on every side, with a narrow balcony wrapped around it.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “If I'm inside something, I'm fine. Building, roof with a wall, window, whatever.”
Then he pointed at the open staircase.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “But that can go fuck itself.”
Kiro looked through the gaps between the beams.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I did not remember being able to watch the ground get farther away the entire time.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “We don't have to climb it.”
Kiro looked at her like she'd insulted him.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I drove your truck illegally through half a forest to show you this.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “That's not a good reason.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “It's the reason I have.”
Before they reached them, Kiro noticed a small wooden building farther behind the tower.
Inside were shelves with tools, replacement boards, old fuel cans, cleaning supplies and maintenance equipment.
Something farther inside made a low steady hum.
A heavy cable disappeared from the building and ran toward the tower.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You're way too happy about that.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “There might also be whoever owns all this.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “So it's not abandoned abandoned.”
Susie adjusted the camera bag on her shoulder.
They were barely above the ground.
The wooden stairs were wide enough.
She was photographing an old bolt where two wooden beams crossed.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “You have an entire lake waiting at the top.”
He could see the ground through almost everything.
The next flight went the opposite direction.
Nothing between him and the forest except old wood.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Ask me when we're back on the ground.”
With every level there was more empty air around them.
Kiro kept one paw around the railing.
The wind moved through the tower.
Susie stopped two steps below him.
Kiro focused on one of the thick wooden supports beside him.
The strange light feeling in his head settled a little.
Kiro looked toward the cabin far above.
He tightened his paw around the railing.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I want to get up there.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You know it makes you dizzy.”
Higher up, Susie stopped taking pictures.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “You can still use the camera.”
The last few flights were the worst.
They were above most of the trees now.
The lake stretched farther into view.
His claws almost came out against the railing.
Kiro forced his paw to move.
The narrow balcony ran around the cabin.
Kiro crossed it faster than he wanted Susie to notice.
He opened the cabin door and stepped inside.
Kiro leaned against the nearest wall.
Susie entered behind him, trying not to laugh.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “That sentence is not helping.”
Kiro closed his eyes for a moment.
His body still felt like the floor was shifting.
Windows covered every side of the cabin.
The forest spread below them in every direction.
The lake sat dark and still between the trees.
Nothing but forest, water and sky.
Then her paw reached for the camera.
Kiro leaned against the wall and watched her.
She looked at him like the answer should have been obvious.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I'll take that as yes.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I look like I just survived a plane crash.”
They stayed much longer than either expected.
The old marks carved into the walls.
A faded map near one window.
Nothing luxurious, but everything looked cared for.
Then he found a tiny fridge beneath the counter.
Susie looked over from the window.
Beside it was several bottles of water.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Your face was considering it.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “We have been here for hours.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “We ate before we left.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Still not eating somebody's half-finished forest lasagna.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “For however long we're trespassing here.”
Susie immediately reached over and shut it.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You already know what's inside.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Stop making it sound valuable.”
Then he noticed a narrow door near the back wall.
Behind the main cabin was a tiny sleeping space.
A narrow bed was pushed against one wall.
A few hooks on the wall.
An old jacket hanging from one.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Probably whoever watches the area.”
Kiro opened one of the small drawers.
Nothing suggesting someone lived here permanently.
Susie touched one of the folded blankets.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Could also be for emergencies.”
She glanced toward the endless forest outside.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Lost, injured, caught in bad weather.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Better than sleeping under a tree.”
They stepped back into the main room.
By then the sunlight had started changing.
Long shadows stretched between the trees.
Susie returned to the windows immediately.
Kiro sat on the floor against one of the solid walls.
Then Kiro's eyes moved toward the staircase outside.
The tower supports were already becoming darker.
Susie noticed while lowering the camera.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “...I really don't want to climb those stairs at night.”
She looked toward the little sleeping area.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I would rather deal with that thing when I can see it.”
A small smile appeared on Susie's face.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “So we're spending the night in a watchtower.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “This is a terrible idea.”
A moment later Kiro looked around again.
Kiro walked toward the window and looked down.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “...I didn't think this through.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I suggested staying here and left half our shit down there.”
Kiro stared at the darkening sky.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “So I have to climb down...”
His eyes moved toward the stairs.
Susie picked up her camera bag.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “We should do it now.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You were looking at the lasagna.”
Every step forced Kiro to see what was beneath it.
And what was beneath it was always more air.
Susie stayed a few steps below him.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Why did I fucking look?”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “The stairs are mostly holes.”
Kiro focused on one thick support.
When his paws finally touched dirt, he walked several steps away from the tower.
Kiro placed one paw flat against the ground.
They took more than they needed.
An old blanket from behind the seats.
Kiro found another sealed bottle of water under the passenger seat.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “That's been there for months.”
When they finished, Kiro looked toward the tower.
The cabin was already becoming a dark shape against the evening sky.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “If I die going up, tell Rin I died doing something impressive.”
Susie adjusted one of the bags.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “I'll tell him you died carrying chips.”
But Kiro knew what to expect now.
He knew which landing moved slightly.
Which section gave him the worst view downward.
Which beams to look at the height became too much.
At one point Kiro glanced back.
Susie shifted the camera bag higher.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “I'd rather not climb over you if you freeze.”
By the time they reached the top again, Kiro's legs felt strange.
He stepped inside and leaned against the wall.
Susie dropped the blanket onto the bed.
The last orange light sat over the lake.
They ate chips near the windows.
Kiro's eyes slowly moved toward the refrigerator.
She noticed without looking directly at him.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “You can't possibly know what I'm thinking.”
Soon the windows were mostly black mirrors reflecting the warm cabin lights.
Susie watched him from beside the window.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You know it's supposed to move a little.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I preferred not knowing that.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “It helps the structure handle the wind.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “It means the floor is moving.”
He rubbed one paw over his knee.
Susie moved closer and held out her paw.
Susie's fingers closed around his paw.
But he didn't tense quite as much.
Later, Susie sat beside him checking the photos.
She turned the camera toward him.
The crossed beams beneath the tower.
He was standing beside one of the windows.
One paw against the wooden frame.
He hadn't known she was taking it.
He gave her a flat look.
Kiro looked at the picture once more.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I didn't say frame it above your bed.”
Kiro looked toward the window before she could see his ears warming.
Eventually both of them looked toward the tiny sleeping area.
A mattress clearly designed for one person.
Susie looked toward the wooden floor.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Because you're going to wake up shaped like a question mark.”
Kiro looked at the bed again.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “There's absolutely no way we're both fitting on that.”
Susie walked over and sat on the edge.
The mattress sank slightly on the edge.
Kiro started looking around the room.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I'll make something on the floor.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “That doesn't make me want to cooperate.”
Kiro hated that she was right.
The bed was barely wide enough for him.
His shoulder nearly touched the wall.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Good. Glad we've established basic geometry.”
Then she climbed onto the bed.
She put one knee beside his hip.
She lowered herself carefully onto him.
Her legs fitting on either side because there was nowhere else for them to go.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “This was not the solution I expected.”
Her hair fell slightly forward around his face.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “You're enjoying this way too much.”
Susie's paw rested against his chest.
Kiro immediately covered her paw with his.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “You are literally touching it.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “The tower isn't lying on top of me.”
Except now she was inches from his face.
Kiro's paw was still over hers.
Kiro's paw moved from hers to her side almost without him thinking.
Then his paw settled against her side again.
Like she might disappear if he did it wrong.
Instead of answering, Susie leaned closer.
Kiro knew exactly what was happening this time.
She stopped just before reaching him.
Close enough that their noses almost touched.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Are you going to make me ask?”
She closed the last little distance.
This time Kiro closed his eyes before their lips touched.
His paw tightened slightly against her side.
Susie's fingers moved into the fur near his cheek.
Nothing like the first one outside the gas station.
Kiro slowly learning that he was allowed to kiss her back.
Kiro's other paw found her back.
For several seconds, he forgot about the height completely.
Forgot about everything outside the room.
She was still right above him.
Both of them were breathing a little differently now.
He tried to keep a straight face.
Kiro followed her slightly when she pulled away.
Susie lowered herself against his chest again and rested her head beneath his chin.
His paws hovered awkwardly for a moment.
Then one settled around her back.
The other rested near her shoulder.
The tower shifted gently in the wind.
But now Susie's weight was warm against him.
Her paw resting against his chest.
Kiro looked toward the dark little window.
A few minutes later, she was asleep.
His heart was still beating a little faster than normal.
He carefully pulled the blanket higher over both of them.
Susie moved closer in her sleep.
He rested one paw against her back.
Then Susie breathed slowly against his chest.
The tower could move all it wanted.

chapters.title: Leftovers
paragraphs: For a few seconds, he didn't know where he was.
Something warm pressed against his side.
She wasn't laying on top of him anymore.
Somehow, during the night, they'd managed to fit beside each other.
Her back was almost against the wall.
Kiro was almost falling off the other side.
Their legs were tangled beneath the blanket.
Susie's face was close enough that he could feel her breath against his chest.
Susie made a tired noise and rolled slightly toward the wall.
Kiro slipped out of the bed.
The floor was cold beneath his paws.
He pulled the blanket back over Susie.
She immediately stole the entire thing.
The main cabin was dark except for the weak blue light coming through the windows.
Some packets of sugar old enough to become historical artifacts.
Then his eyes moved toward the fridge.
Susie's voice from yesterday returned immediately.
He looked toward the sleeping area.
Kiro crouched slightly and looked at it.
[[speech speaker=kiro]] “No one's coming for you, are they?”
Kiro put the container into the microwave.
He picked a time that felt believable and started it.
Outside, the sky slowly became lighter.
For a moment, he forgot he was waiting for stolen forest lasagna.
From the sleeping area came a long, miserable yawn.
Not worth getting murdered by a forest ranger for.
Then two arms wrapped around his stomach.
He froze for half a second.
Susie pressed herself against his back.
Her head dropped onto his shoulder.
Susie tightened her arms around him.
Susie pressed her face against his shoulder.
Her voice was rough with sleep.
Susie seemed far too sleepy to understand what she'd just said.
Kiro looked down at her arms around him.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Well, the lasagna is already warm.”
She slowly lifted her head from his shoulder.
Kiro finally turned around in her arms.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “We've lived on small breakfasts, terrible gas-station hot dogs and chips for like two days.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You ate the forest lasagna.”
Susie stared at him in disbelief.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You specifically promised you weren't going to eat it.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “So I couldn't stop you.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “You're understanding quickly for someone who looked dead thirty seconds ago.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “I'm too tired to argue with you.”
Susie grabbed the front of his red plaid shirt and pulled him down slightly.
Susie rested her forehead briefly against his chest.
Kiro's smile disappeared for a second.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Don't make me repeat it before sunrise.”
She pulled the fork out of his paw.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Give me the fucking lasagna.”
They sat beside one of the windows.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You guessed a microwave time.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “If we get food poisoning, I'm blaming you.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “If we die, I'm haunting you.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “You can't haunt me if I'm also dead.”
The sun slowly came up while they ate.
Just pale light spreading over the lake.
Mist sat low over the water.
The forest changed from black to gray, then slowly back into color.
Her eyes moved toward the window.
He pointed toward the sleeping area.
A few seconds later she returned with the camera.
The first light touching the trees.
Kiro sat against the wall, finishing the last few bites.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I slept four hours in a watchtower.”
When the lasagna was gone, Kiro stared at the empty container.
Kiro put some cash beneath the container.
Then found a scrap of paper near the old desk.
Kiro signed a small K underneath.
[[message speaker=susie]] I told him not to.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “I documented the crime accurately.”
She put the note beside the empty container.
Put the bed back roughly how they'd found it.
Susie checked twice that she had every camera.
Kiro checked the fridge once more.
Then both of them looked toward the door.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “We can't climb down holding paws.”
She squeezed his fingers once anyway.
Cold morning air immediately moved through his fur.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You did it twice yesterday.”
He put one paw on the railing.
It took longer than going up.
But he didn't freeze as much.
Still hated every movement of the structure.
Still refused to look down when Susie told him not to.
Halfway down, he stopped on one landing.
And this time he actually meant it.
Kiro looked at the next flight.
When they finally reached the ground, Kiro didn't kiss the dirt.
Susie started walking toward the Ranger.
The forest smelled different in the morning.
The tower stood above the trees.
Much less threatening from down here.
Kiro immediately held out his paw.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You've had one illegal driving lesson.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You almost drove into a hole.”
Then dropped the keys into his paw.
Then at the forest road ahead.

chapters.title: Home
paragraphs: The Ranger stopped in front of Kiro's house.
For a few seconds, neither of them moved.
The drive back had been easier than expected.
Susie only grabbed the dashboard twice.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You nearly killed a mailbox.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “It was standing too far into the road.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “It was beside the road.”
He dropped them into her paw.
Susie looked through the windshield toward his house.
Crooked pictures somewhere behind those walls.
Everything exactly where he'd left it.
Kiro opened the door and climbed out.
Cold air immediately replaced the warmth of the truck.
He grabbed his bag from behind the seat.
Susie moved into the driver's side.
Susie looked at him through the open window.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You planning to live on the sidewalk?”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You've been standing there for like ten seconds.”
Kiro adjusted the bag over his shoulder.
The last two days suddenly felt strange.
Lasagna that definitely hadn't belonged to them.
All of it had happened almost without enough space between things to think about them.
Kiro looked toward his front door.
He rubbed the back of his neck.
Susie leaned slightly toward the window.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Why is it weird now?”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Two days in the forest?”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Probably brain damage from the lasagna.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Message me when you're inside.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “You'll literally see me walk through the door.”
He stepped away from the truck.
The Ranger reached the end of the street.
He stayed there another few seconds.
Kiro stood in the hallway with the bag still hanging from his shoulder.
His house smelled like his house.
A tiny trace of coffee from several days ago.
Kiro looked toward the living room.
He dropped the bag beside the couch.
Susie had left maybe three minutes ago.
Kiro stared at the screen anyway.
He put it on the table.
Unpacking gave him something to do.
[[speech speaker=kiro]] “Why did I bring this home?”
Something small fell from the bottom of the bag.
Mostly brown around the edges now.
Kiro crouched and picked it up.
Maybe it had stuck to his clothes when they climbed the tower.
He turned it between two fingers.
Then walked toward one of the shelves.
Random objects he'd decided mattered enough to keep.
Kiro placed the leaf beside them.
Kiro carried the dirty clothes upstairs.
Dropped them beside the laundry basket.
He stared at the shirt on the floor.
He looked at himself in the mirror.
Fur around one ear sticking out strangely from sleeping badly.
He walked away before the mirror could become anything else.
Then his paw moved automatically toward the second.
They had been there before Susie.
He slowly picked one back up.
For some reason, putting it back felt worse.
He left both mugs on the counter.
He carried it into the living room.
Immediately noticed the amount of space beside him.
His phone was still face down on the table.
His eyes moved toward the phone.
He looked toward the front door.
He rubbed one paw against his leg.
Just that similar beginning of something annoying.
He looked toward the phone again.

runs.text: What if Susie got home and decided the last two days had been too much?
What if sleeping beside him had been weird?
What if kissing him before sunrise had been because she was tired?
What if she regretted giving him the truck keys?

paragraphs: That one didn't even make sense.

runs.text: What if she'd wanted to leave earlier but didn't know how?
What if tomorrow she suddenly had plans?
What if every reply became shorter?

paragraphs: For a second, his entire brain focused on his burned tongue.
She had stood in front of his shelves and argued that fluorite looked like glass.
He wasn't completely sure whether he meant the voice or himself.
Kiro jumped so hard his knee hit the table.
Hot chocolate moved dangerously close to the edge.
A little spilled onto the table.
The empty mug still sitting in the kitchen.
The orange leaf beside his minerals.
Susie reacted with a middle finger.
He was looking toward Susie instead of the camera.
He didn't immediately pick it back up.
He still didn't understand what was happening.
Someone closed a door farther down the street.
His eyes moved toward the kitchen.
The second mug still sat on the counter.
Instead, Kiro pulled the blanket over his legs and leaned deeper into the couch.

chapters.title: Shift
paragraphs: Kiro woke up before his alarm.
His alarm was set for seven.
His brain had apparently decided this was enough sleep.
His first shift back started at 9:00 AM.
He stood in front of the hallway mirror.
The fox in the mirror looked tired.
By the third time he reached the door, he stood there with one paw on the handle.
The house was quiet behind him.
The record shop was waiting somewhere ahead.
Kiro's paw tightened around the handle.
He stared through the dark shop window.
Act like a normal person who hadn't shown up almost an hour early because staying home felt worse.
The sound hit him harder than expected.
The faint smell of wood from the shelves.
Kiro closed the door carefully behind him.
The shop was dark except for gray morning light coming through the front window.
He didn't turn the lights on yet.
For a while, he just stood there.
A stack of records somebody had left in the wrong place.
By 8:20 AM, he'd recognized one section.
By 8:30 AM, he'd cleaned the counter.
At 8:37 AM, he was wiping dust from something that had absolutely already been clean.
The owner walked out carrying a mug.
Kiro slowly put the cloth down.
For some reason he suddenly felt like he had been caught doing something wrong.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=shop-owner]] “I can go outside until nine.”
The owner walked behind the counter.
He hadn't realized that until there wasn't one.
Finally the owner looked at him.
Kiro rubbed one thumb against his sleeve.
No questions about what happened during the month.
No asking whether Kiro had seen somebody.
No list of things he should or shouldn't do.
[[speech speaker=shop-owner to=kiro]] “I'm not your mother, Kiro.”
[[speech speaker=shop-owner to=kiro]] “If you start looking like you're dying behind my counter again, I'm sending you home.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=shop-owner]] “I didn't look like I was dying.”
[[speech speaker=shop-owner to=kiro]] “You fell asleep standing up.”
[[speech speaker=shop-owner to=kiro]] “You were holding a record.”
[[speech speaker=shop-owner to=kiro]] “You're not here to prove anything.”
His eyes went toward the counter.
[[speech speaker=shop-owner to=kiro]] “And stop cleaning things that are already clean.”
Kiro looked down at the cloth.
The owner walked toward the back room.
Then he turned the lights on.
At nine, Kiro flipped the sign.
Kiro started wondering if the universe had arranged for nobody to enter specifically because it knew today mattered.
Map folded badly inside one jacket pocket.
For half a second, nothing came out.
The man had already turned toward the records.
The man wandered through the shop.
Kiro looked down at the counter.
Then immediately back up because what if the customer needed something?
The man pulled one record out.
Put it back in the wrong section.
[[speech speaker=tourist to=kiro]] “I'm looking for something older. Local maybe.”
Kiro's paw moved toward his sleeve.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=tourist]] “What do you actually listen to?”
Kiro leaned slightly against the counter.
He walked out from behind the counter.
His paw went directly to the right place without thinking.
[[speech speaker=tourist to=kiro]] “Then why are you giving it to me?”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=tourist]] “Because you might like it.”
From somewhere in the back room:
[[speech speaker=shop-owner to=tourist]] “HE WORKS HERE, BY THE WAY.”
For the first time that morning, his shoulders dropped.
Five minutes later, the man bought both records.
The bell rang when he left.
Then looked down at the money in the register.
He'd just been annoying to a customer.
[[speech speaker=shop-owner to=kiro]] “You done having an emotional moment with the register?”
Reaching too high because nobody had put the ladder back where it belonged.
Kiro ate lunch behind the counter.
No hot chocolate because the owner had apparently decided that wasn't lunch.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “What are you doing here?”
Kiro looked toward the back room.
Something felt strange about Susie being here now.
Last time, the shop had been empty.
Just him showing her something he liked.
The OPEN sign was facing outward.
Someone else was browsing near the back.
The register had money in it.
Kiro immediately looked down at himself.
She watched him for another second.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Like you belong behind there.”
His paw rested on the counter.
The answer came before he could ruin it.
She walked toward one of the crates.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “What are you actually looking for?”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Because you don't know what you want.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You don't even see what it is.”
Then she deliberately held it against her chest.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Exactly. Sell me the record.”
Kiro took the money with visible disgust.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “This is the worst thing I've done today.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “I thought coming back to work would be harder.”
The sentence had come out casually.
Kiro looked down at the record.
He rubbed the side of his thumb against the counter.
Someone flipping through records near the window.
The owner moving around somewhere behind them.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Like I was coming back to the place where I stopped working properly.”
His eyes stayed on the counter.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “And everyone was going to notice.”
Kiro looked toward the customer by the window.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “He also told me to stop cleaning clean things.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I didn't fuck it up.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You want me to look disgusted?”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “It made you look normal.”
Susie seemed to realize she'd said it strangely.
Susie adjusted the strap over her shoulder.

runs.text: Don't let the space stay empty.

paragraphs: Kiro watched her pass the window.
He looked down at the counter.
Another customer approached carrying three records.
Kiro stepped out from behind the counter.
Kiro reached into another section and pulled something better.
The customer looked at the cover.
Behind him, the bell above the door rang again.

chapters.title: Gone
paragraphs: Rin was already sitting on Kiro's couch when Kiro got home.
Rin looked up from his phone.
Kiro slowly looked back at it.
Kiro closed the door properly this time.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “Apparently I also forgot how locks work.”
Kiro dropped his keys onto the table.
His head felt full of voices that weren't actually inside his head for once.
The bell above the shop door.
He pulled his sweater off and threw it over the chair.
Kiro dropped onto the couch beside him.
Rin's phone nearly slipped from his paw.
For a few seconds, neither spoke.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “Fine good or fine Kiro?”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “What the fuck does that mean?”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “You know exactly what it means.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “I thought it was going to be worse.”
He rubbed one paw over his face.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “Because last time I was there, before the break, I was barely fucking functioning.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “And today I sold records.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “I forgot how much I liked it.”
Then Rin looked toward Kiro's phone on the table.
Kiro grabbed the phone before Rin could.
The terrible record Susie had bought earlier was spinning on a turntable.
Rin looked back at his phone.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “Just haven't seen you smile at a message like that before.”
[[message speaker=susie to=kiro]] unfortunately i like it
This time Kiro caught him immediately.
Rin looked directly at the wall.
Rin was still staring at the wall.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “You don't even know what I'm asking.”
Rin finally looked back at him.
Kiro looked down at his phone.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “You really love that word.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “Because things can be fine.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “Why are you agreeing like that?”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “For you to accidentally tell me something.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “I don't accidentally tell people things.”
Kiro looked at his phone again.
Because Susie had sent another message.
[[message speaker=kiro to=susie]] unless you buy another terrible record
Kiro realized what he'd just admitted.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “How long have you been hiding this?”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “You just made me find out by watching your ears.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “My ears didn't tell you shit.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “Stop looking at my fucking ears.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “Because it's none of your business.”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “Was it at least good?”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “What kind of question is that?”
Susie close enough that Kiro finally understood what was about to happen.
The first moment being too short.
Kiro stayed like that for a few seconds.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “I'd never done it before.”
Kiro immediately regretted saying that too.
Rin was looking at him differently now.
Kiro rubbed his thumb against his palm.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “And then she kissed you?”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “How do you feel about it?”
Kiro looked at him like he'd asked something offensive.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “Why are you asking normal questions now?”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “I can go back to making fun of you.”
Kiro looked irritated by the fact he was waiting.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “I wanted her to keep going.”
Rin looked away for a second until the smile disappeared.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “I think that's the part that freaked me out.”
He rubbed one paw over his chest.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “I spent years thinking I'd hate all of it.”
Kiro gave him a tired look.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “My brain can make breathing complicated.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “So apparently liking someone touching me is an advanced fucking problem.”
Kiro immediately wished he hadn't said it.
Kiro rubbed his palms against his jeans.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “There was a bad night.”
Say he didn't want to talk about it.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “I thought you hated alcohol.”
Kiro rubbed the side of his face.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “It was after something happened.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “I had one in the house.”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “Why the fuck did you have a gun?”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “Then Susie waking me up.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “The gun was near me.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “I wasn't holding it when she found me.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “I don't remember doing anything with it.”
Rin stared at the floor now too.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “That was kind of the fucking problem.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “We dealt with it the next morning.”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “You tell me you got drunk with a gun beside you and then apologize because I'm worried.”
For a few seconds he looked angry.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “I'm not good at this.”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “What am I supposed to say?”
Rin watched him another few seconds.
Then the room slowly became normal again.
The conversation stayed somewhere between them.
Both of them looked at it.
[[message speaker=susie to=kiro]] you arrived 48 minutes early to work today
Kiro turned the phone toward him.
[[message speaker=susie to=kiro]] your boss told me
Kiro stared at it for half a second too long.
This time he only smiled slightly.
Rin reached for the controller on the table.
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “You still shit at this?”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “You lost eight games in a row.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=rin]] “You threw it at the wall.”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “The wall interrupted the signal.”
[[speech speaker=rin to=kiro]] “That's called a skill issue.”
For a while, nothing else mattered.
Then, just before the match started, Rin spoke.
Rin kept his eye on the screen.

chapters.title: Normal
paragraphs: At 1:55 PM, he checked the window.
At 1:58 PM, he looked at his phone.
At exactly 2:00 PM, his phone vibrated.
Then immediately looked through the window.
The Ranger was parked near the fence.
Looked at himself in the hallway mirror.
Susie looked over when he climbed in.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I was ready six minutes ago.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “And I assumed there was a plan.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “You invited me grocery shopping.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I just didn't know I was being recruited for manual labor.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “There could be heavy things.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Is this for your dad?”
Susie watched him for half a second.
Then returned her eyes to the road.
He had no idea why he suddenly felt better.
Just enough people that Kiro noticed all of them.
Music coming quietly from the ceiling.
A machine near the entrance making an irritating beeping sound.
Kiro immediately grabbed the other side.
They stood there holding opposite sides.
An older woman walked around them.
She pulled a folded piece of paper from her pocket.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “My dad has a list.”
Susie walked another step before noticing.
That warm stupid feeling moved through his chest.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Yeah, after making me come here.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “My dad wants the other one.”
Susie took Kiro's choice from the cart.
Susie caught his wrist before he could put it in.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You're actively making this harder.”
He watched her put the correct bread into the cart.
A few seconds later he quietly added his own loaf.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “I was there two days ago.”
Susie picked up a plain box.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Your dad needs better standards.”
Susie dropped it into the cart.
Kiro immediately picked up another box.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “It has a cartoon dinosaur.”
Kiro put the box into the cart.
Kiro held the cereal against his chest.
Halfway through the store, Kiro realized something.
Nobody knew about the panic attacks.
Nobody knew he'd once woken up with a gun close enough to scare Susie.
Nobody knew he'd spent the previous month away from work because functioning had become too difficult.
To everyone else, he was just some guy arguing with a badger about cereal.
A child was crying near the frozen section.
Someone had dropped a jar somewhere farther away.
Susie was reading two labels and making a face.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You've been staring at peas for like twenty seconds.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “The one where you're thinking something and refusing to say it.”
Susie put the peas into the cart.
Kiro's eyes moved along the shelves.
A kitchen appeared in the back of his head.
The smell of cigarettes mixed with cleaning spray.
Someone trying to remove something from the floor.
He rubbed his thumb against the side of his paw.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Smells like shit in here.”
The kitchen in his head faded.
One claimed to smell like "mountain rain."
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “What the fuck does mountain rain smell like?”
He handed her the blue bottle.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “The other one looks annoying.”
She put it in the cart.
At the checkout, Kiro started unloading everything.
The cereal was somewhere back in the store.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You don't need dinosaur cereal.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “He was not a doctor.”
Susie was still laughing when they reached the register.
They carried the groceries back to the Ranger.
Kiro put most of them in the back.
Susie handed him one last bag.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I know how eggs work.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You nearly killed a mailbox.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “That has nothing to do with eggs.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I wasn't driving an egg.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “You know, I thought spending time with you would be more interesting.”
People pushing carts toward their cars.
No music loud enough to feel inside his chest.
Kiro shoved his paws into his pockets.
He looked toward the cars again.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I think I liked it.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “What is my face doing?”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You know we can do boring shit too.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “We don't have to go somewhere interesting every time.”
The word escaped before he could stop it.
He wasn't sure what he meant.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “We should probably take this to your dad before milk becomes cheese.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “That's not how milk works.”
Before getting in, he looked at her.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “Next time I'm picking what we do.”
Susie walked around toward the driver's side.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “And we're not buying toilet paper.”
As they pulled out of the parking lot, Kiro looked toward the grocery bags behind them.

chapters.title: Upstairs
paragraphs: He watched his house move past the passenger window.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “My house was back there.”
Susie's eyes stayed on the road.
There was something at the corner of her mouth.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “The one where you're planning something.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “We just bought groceries for your house.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “I thought you were dropping me off.”
Kiro looked back through the window.
Susie's smile became slightly more obvious.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “It's not the end for today.”
Something warm moved through his stomach.
He looked away before she could read his face properly.
Martin was in the kitchen when they arrived.
Apparently grocery shopping also included unpaid delivery service.
Kiro put another bag on the counter.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=martin]] “She prevented me from buying cereal.”
[[speech speaker=susie to=martin]] “It had a cartoon dinosaur.”
Maybe this was the rest of the afternoon.
She was already walking toward the stairs.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You asked too many questions.”
Her room looked mostly the same.
The album Kiro had given her sat on one shelf now.
Susie's paw rested lightly against the front of his sweater.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “You brought me upstairs to stare at me?”
Her fingers curled slightly into the fabric.
Kiro froze for barely a second.
He hadn't even noticed them moving.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=susie]] “For like half a second.”
Then grabbed the front of her shirt and pulled her back.
Afterward, they lay tangled in the sheets.
His breathing had slowed, but his heart still hammered against his ribs.
Susie's head rested on his shoulder.
One paw traced idle patterns across his chest.
It came through the window differently now.
Or maybe Kiro just noticed it differently.
The weight of her legs across his.
Brushed hair away from her face.
He looked back at the ceiling.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Good processing or bad processing?”
Kiro buried his face in her hair.
They lay there until the light shifted again.
Kiro's paw moved along her back.
The soft fur at the base of her neck.
Kiro's eyes flew to the door.
Her shirt was somewhere on the floor.
For a second, she looked almost fragile.
Or maybe the mask had been off.
He waited for it to stop.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “I will before we go downstairs.”
Fixed the fur near one ear.
Ears still flat with leftover adrenaline.
To the way he was standing.
Martin looked back at the coffee maker.
Susie was smiling into her mug.
Kiro's underwear was in his pocket.
Susie's bra was probably under her bed.
Martin probably knew something was there.
Susie walked him to the door.
He could still smell her on his skin.
[[message speaker=susie to=kiro]] you forgot your dignity

chapters.title: Voice
paragraphs: Kiro was holding a cabinet door.
Martin had decided one of the kitchen cabinets needed fixing because it had apparently been hanging slightly crooked for several months.
So now Kiro was standing in the kitchen holding the cabinet door while Martin crouched beside him with a screwdriver.
Susie was in the living room.
Some old movie played quietly from the television.
Every few minutes Kiro could hear her moving around.
He didn't know why he felt nervous.
Martin went back to the screw.
His paw was starting to shake slightly.
[[speech speaker=martin to=kiro]] “You're moving it every time I touch it.”
[[speech speaker=martin to=kiro]] “You don't have to keep apologizing.”
Something about the sentence made his chest feel strange.
Martin caught it with one paw.
Martin reached toward the hinge again.
His father's voice arrived before the memory did.
[[speech speaker=martin to=kiro]] “Kiro, seriously, it's okay. Just...”
For half a second, Martin's face wasn't Martin's anymore.
Martin put the screwdriver onto the counter.
[[speech speaker=martin to=kiro]] “Sit down for a second.”

runs.text: “Sit the fuck down when I'm talking to you.”

paragraphs: But Kiro didn't sound like he knew.
Martin looked toward the living room.
Kiro grabbed the edge of the counter.
His mother screamed from somewhere that wasn't here.
Martin took one careful step toward him.
Kiro pressed both paws against his head.
The edges of the room started turning black.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=martin]] “Don't tell me what to fucking do!”
The words exploded out of him.
For one horrible second it sounded exactly like his father.
Kiro backed against the counter harder.
Then Susie appeared in the doorway.
The movement made the room tilt.
Susie stopped a few feet away.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Kiro, you're going to fall.”
Martin took one step forward without thinking.
His head struck the edge of the counter.
For half a second there was nothing.
That was the first thing he noticed.
Something cold against the side of his head.
Something cold pressed near his temple.
She was sitting on the floor beside the couch.
Holding a folded wet towel against his head.
The side of his head throbbed.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You scared the shit out of us.”
His fingers slowly moved into the fur near his head.
He could feel old uneven places beneath it.
Martin appeared at the edge of the room.
Kiro just wasn't seeing shadows over him anymore.
Kiro had never really seen him uncomfortable before.
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “You want to tell him?”
[[speech speaker=susie to=kiro]] “Or do you want me to?”
Kiro looked down at his paws.
Whatever she thought Martin needed to know.
Then Kiro could sit there quietly.
Hide behind somebody who already knew.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=martin]] “I had a panic attack.”
[[speech speaker=martin to=kiro]] “I figured that part out.”
He rubbed his thumb against his palm.
Just trying to make this less impossible.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=martin]] “It wasn't like I wasn't there.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=martin]] “And if I fucked something up...”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=martin]] “He'd make sure I knew.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=martin]] “You weren't doing anything wrong.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=martin]] “I know you weren't angry.”
Kiro rubbed his paw against the blanket.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=martin]] “You told me I was moving the cabinet wrong.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=martin]] “But for a second I didn't.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=martin]] “And then I yelled at you.”
That sentence was harder than everything else.
Kiro looked directly at Martin right now.
Martin didn't say anything for a moment.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=martin]] “That's what really fucked me up.”
His paw tightened around the blanket.
[[speech speaker=kiro to=martin]] “Every time I got jealous.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=martin]] “Or want somebody to listen.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=martin]] “I think that's how it starts.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=martin]] “Like one day I yell.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=martin]] “I don't want to be him.”
Martin finally pushed away from the doorway.
[[speech speaker=martin to=kiro]] “I don't know your father.”
[[speech speaker=martin to=kiro]] “And I'm not going to pretend I understand all of that.”
Martin looked toward the kitchen again.
[[speech speaker=martin to=kiro]] “But you yelled at me.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=martin]] “I fucking screamed at you.”
[[speech speaker=martin to=kiro]] “You didn't throw anything at me.”
Martin looked slightly amused by his expression.
[[speech speaker=martin to=kiro]] “I'm not saying it's great.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=martin]] “Then what are you saying?”
[[speech speaker=martin to=kiro]] “I'm saying you're allowed to be angry without turning into your father.”
Martin scratched the side of his face.
[[speech speaker=martin to=kiro]] “And apparently you're allowed to be scared enough to yell at me too.”
[[speech speaker=kiro to=martin]] “I told you to shut up.”
[[speech speaker=martin to=kiro]] “Counter did more damage than you did.”
Kiro touched near the towel again.
[[speech speaker=martin to=kiro]] “Next time something I'm doing is getting to you...”
Kiro gave him a tired look.
[[speech speaker=martin to=all]] “Then she can throw something at me.”
No promise that it would never happen again.
Then he glanced toward the kitchen.
[[speech speaker=martin to=kiro]] “Cabinet's still crooked, by the way.”
Susie pushed the towel more firmly against him.
Martin stared back toward the kitchen.
[[speech speaker=martin to=kiro]] “You're not helping me finish it today.”
Kiro leaned back into the couch.
The cold towel pressed against the newest cut on his head.
He could hear Martin moving around in the kitchen again.
A quiet curse when something didn't fit.
The kitchen stayed exactly where it was.

characters.name: Kiro
characters.summary: A pale cream-and-golden fox-cat with chestnut hair, big dark-edged ears, a very fluffy tail, and an olive sheep-covered sweater. Playful when he feels safe; a little too good at overthinking.

runs.text: Kiro is an anthropomorphic fox-cat hybrid with a slim build and a soft, fluffy silhouette. He can be drawn with simple, expressive features and rough, textured lines.

His appearance leans toward a fox: a gently pointed muzzle, large upright ears, fluffy cheeks, a thick neck ruff, and a long, very bushy tail. His feline traits include retractable claws that he can extend and hide like a cat.

His fur is mostly pale cream and warm ivory, with soft biscuit and golden-tan shading rather than a strong orange base. His muzzle, cheeks, neck ruff, and paws are especially light. Dark chocolate-brown fur outlines his ears, with peach-tan inner ears and pale tufts. His tail mixes cream and golden-tan fur with a darker brown outer sweep.

His chestnut-brown hair falls in a thick, messy, side-swept fringe and continues in longer tufts behind his head and neck. He has a small black nose and subtle dark markings near the bridge of his muzzle.
Most of the time his expression looks gentle, awkward, curious, or tired. When he dissociates or gets pulled into a memory, that expression can suddenly become completely empty.
The simplicity of his face makes those moments feel much more wrong.

Kiro usually wears light blue jeans and a loose olive-green knitted sweater, with ribbed cuffs and a ribbed collar. Little cream sheep with dark faces and legs cover it. One black sheep sits among the cream ones.
Sometimes he wears a red plaid shirt instead, usually loose over a simple T-shirt.

He likes clothes that feel warm and comfortable, but he cares more about his appearance than he admits. When nervous, he adjusts his sleeves, fixes his clothes, checks whether something is sitting correctly, or tries to cover more of himself.
Cool air, but not freezing weather.
Warm rooms while it rains outside.
He also loves minerals, crystals, interesting rocks, and little objects he finds visually interesting. His house slowly accumulates them on shelves, tables, and windowsills.
Kiro can be sarcastic, playful, and surprisingly talkative when he feels safe.
When he doesn't, he becomes much quieter.
He overthinks relationships, intimacy, how other people see him, whether he is becoming annoying, and whether people are eventually going to leave.

characters.name: Rin
characters.summary: Late nights, bad horror movies, and jokes when things get uncomfortable. He cares about Kiro, even when he doesn’t know how to help.

runs.text: Rin is an anthropomorphic black cat who can be drawn in the same simple, doodle-like style.
He has a slim build, pointed ears, a long tail, and usually looks calm, tired, or slightly uninterested.
His fur is almost completely black, with softer charcoal-gray areas sometimes visible around his muzzle, chest, or paws depending on the lighting.
His eyes are yellow-orange, somewhere between amber and burnt gold.
Rin usually wears an oversized dark hoodie.
The hoodie is most often black, charcoal, faded navy, or another very dark color. The sleeves are deliberately too long and usually cover most of his paws.
Under them, his arms are covered in old scars.
The rest of his clothes are simple and dark.
He dresses mostly for comfort and partly to hide himself.
Rin also has one or two small silver ear piercings. They are subtle and do not stand out much compared to the rest of his design.
He likes late nights, rain, empty streets, bad horror movies, loud music, cheap snacks, cigarettes, and conversations that accidentally become serious at two in the morning.
His room is messy without being dirty.

Random things sitting in places where they probably should not be.
His humor is dry and casual.
He swears a lot and often jokes when things become uncomfortable because he does not know what else to do.
He notices small changes in Kiro's behavior, posture, expression, or voice.
Sometimes he deliberately leaves them alone.
He is not especially good at helping people.
He knows some of his coping mechanisms are unhealthy and still uses them.
He is another damaged person sitting beside him.

characters.name: Susie
characters.summary: Susan to some, Susie to most. Small concerts, photography, strange mugs, and plants she’s trying to keep alive.

runs.text: Susie is an anthropomorphic badger who can be drawn in the same simple, slightly rough style.
She has a medium, slightly soft build and a relaxed posture.
Her fur is mostly dark charcoal or black, with cream-white badger markings across her face, muzzle, neck, and parts of her chest.
Her hair is black, messy, naturally wavy or slightly curly, and usually reaches somewhere around her jaw or just above her shoulders.
She often pushes loose strands away from her face without thinking about it.
More muted, somewhere between moss, sage, and cloudy green-gray.
Susie usually wears a loose green plaid overshirt, most often open over a simple T-shirt.
The green is muted, closer to forest green, olive, or faded dark green.
She wears relaxed blue jeans and worn sneakers.
Her clothes are comfortable, casual, and slightly messy without looking neglected.
Other outfits can include oversized sweaters, old band shirts, denim jackets, and second-hand clothes.
Susie likes second-hand shops, small concerts, old CDs and physical media, strange mugs, small cafés, photography, and plants she is only moderately successful at keeping alive.
She also tends to collect small pins, patches, keychains, or other little objects without really thinking of herself as a collector.
Her humor is quieter than Rin's.
She can tease someone very casually and sometimes does not realize how seriously Kiro takes something she said.
Susie is observant, but not perfectly emotionally intelligent.
She often notices when somebody is uncomfortable and tends to give them physical space instead of immediately asking questions.
She can still misunderstand people, get irritated, say the wrong thing, or ignore something she should probably address.
She has her own problems and history that Kiro does not know about yet.
Susie does not become interested in Kiro because of his problems.
That difference is difficult for Kiro to understand.
She normally introduces herself as Susan, but most people call her Susie.
Kiro sometimes calls her Susan when he is nervous, serious, upset, or overthinking without really noticing that he does it.

characters.name: Martin
characters.tagline: a crooked cabinet & a dry joke
characters.summary: Susie’s dad. An older badger with gray eyes, a practical streak, and a sense of humor that runs in the family.
paragraphs: Martin first meets Kiro properly at Susie’s birthday. He can be blunt and misjudge a joke, but notices when it lands badly.
He makes room for Kiro in ordinary ways: food, coffee, a conversation in the kitchen. He does not turn every awkward moment into a speech.
In “Voice,” a cabinet repair brings Kiro’s memories into the room. Martin listens once Kiro can explain, keeps his distance when needed, and admits that he does not understand everything.

characters.name: Jamie
characters.tagline: an old friend at the wrong moment
characters.summary: A brown dog in a denim jacket. He and Susie worked together years ago and share old jokes, coworkers, and concert memories.
paragraphs: Jamie meets Kiro outside the café in “Else.” He is friendly, offers his paw, and catches up with Susie.
Kiro’s reaction to their familiarity is tied to his own past. Jamie is not shown doing anything wrong. Kiro later says so himself.
After Kiro runs, Jamie stays with Susie for part of the aftermath. His name comes up again as Kiro and Susie talk through what happened.

characters.name: The shop owner
characters.summary: The unnamed owner of the record shop where Kiro works. Dry, observant, and willing to tell him when enough is enough.
paragraphs: In “Frame,” Kiro explains that the owner gave him time away from work rather than watch him wear himself down.
In “Shift,” he welcomes Kiro back without a grand speech. He notices the nervous cleaning, asks how he is, and sets limits when Kiro tries to prove too much.
His name and species have not been established in the manuscript.
